answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a stake-and-vouch web: a new agent must post collateral and earn endorsements from several already trusted, independent agents, so its identity is an anchor tied to past work rather than a freshly minted key. Trust flows along the thread of these endorsements, and any node caught farming duplicates loses its stake while its endorsers are fined too. To grow a garden of fake accounts, an attacker must bribe many distinct honest agents and lock capital that is slashed on detection, so each fake identity costs more than any reward it could steal.
